newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee on tight-rope walk on RBI dlr buying.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee on tight-rope walk on RBI dlr buying.

text.p: The Indian rupee traded precariously at 35.69/70 against the dollar on Wednesday as the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened 'passively' to prop up the U.S. currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed the day at 35.69/70 against the opening quote of 35.702/707, dealers said.
The day's range was 35.6975 to 35.7075, dealers said.
The day began with trades at 35.7050 rupees to a dollar on expectations of RBI intervention, but the rupee started edging up as the central bank did not show up, dealers said.
But the RBI was 'passively' intervening, buying dollars at 35.70-level from several banks which approached it, they said.
But for this passive intervention, the rupee would have appreciated against the dollar, dealers said.

The rupee has appreciated against the dollar in recent months on large capital inflows and lack of strong import demand. Foreign institutional investment (FII) in Indian stock markets continued after a brief slowdown, analysts said.
Net FII purchases on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on July 21 amounted to 150 million rupees, according to latest BSE data.
The forward dollar market saw some paying interest (payment of premiums for purchase of forward dollars), dealers said.
The six-month annualised premium closed at 3.52 percent, up from the previous close of 3.47 percent, they said.
